tec-encryption.summary: Encryption turns data on laptops, servers, databases and backups into unreadable code, and key management keeps the keys apart from that data.
tec-encryption.protects: Customer and staff personal data, card and payment data, backups and archives, against loss or theft of devices and media, insider copying of raw files, and cloud provider or operator access.
tec-encryption.placement: Agent or built-in feature on every laptop and desktop (BitLocker, FileVault); database and storage encryption on servers; backup software encryption; a key manager and hardware security modules (HSMs) in the data centre core or as a cloud HSM service. Owned by Infrastructure, keys custodied by Security.
tec-encryption.how: Each device, database or backup set is encrypted with a data key. Data keys are wrapped by a master key held in a key manager or HSM that never releases it in clear. Recovery keys are escrowed centrally so a lost password does not mean lost data.
pareto: Full-disk encryption on 100% of laptops, with recovery keys escrowed centrally and reported
Encrypted backups, with keys kept away from the backup system and an offline copy of the key material
Transparent database encryption (TDE) on databases holding personal or payment data
One key manager (HSM-backed for payment and signing keys) with key rotation, dual control and an inventory of every key
TLS 1.2 or higher everywhere in transit, with an inventory of certificates and their expiry

tec-encryption.architecture: Endpoints report encryption status and escrow recovery keys to the endpoint manager. Databases, storage arrays and backup software call the key manager over KMIP or PKCS#11. The key manager sits in the restricted core zone of the primary data centre as an HA pair of HSMs, with a third HSM at DR replicating key material. Cloud workloads use the cloud KMS with customer-managed keys, or connect to the on-premises key manager. All key events go to the SIEM.

tec-dlp.summary: Data loss prevention (DLP) spots sensitive data leaving by email, web, cloud upload, USB or print, and warns, blocks or records it.
tec-dlp.protects: Customer personal data, account and card numbers, source code, Board and strategy papers; against careless sharing, insider theft and data copied out by malware.
tec-dlp.placement: Agent on every endpoint; policy in the email gateway and the secure web gateway or SSE/CASB service; cloud API connectors for Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. Policy owned by the data owner and the CISO; tooling run by the security operations or tooling team.
tec-dlp.how: Policies describe sensitive data with patterns (PAN, Aadhaar, account numbers), dictionaries, labels from the classification tool and document fingerprints. Each channel inspects content in motion and applies the policy: log, warn the user, ask for a reason, encrypt or block. Incidents go to a console and the SIEM for review.
pareto: Start in monitor mode on three to five high-value data types (Aadhaar, PAN, card, account numbers, customer lists)
Cover email and web/cloud upload first; they carry most leaks
USB and removable media blocked by default, with an approved-exception process
Use classification labels as the main trigger, not only regex
A weekly incident review with business owners, then move tuned rules to block

tec-classify.summary: A discovery and classification tool scans file shares, databases, email and cloud stores to find where sensitive data really lives, and labels it.
tec-classify.protects: Personal data under DPDP, payment and account data, confidential business documents; against over-sharing, forgotten copies, excess retention and blind spots in DLP and access control.
tec-classify.placement: Scanners in the data centre (near file servers and databases) and API connectors to cloud services (Microsoft 365, Google, AWS, Azure); labelling add-in on user devices. Owned by the data protection officer or data governance lead, run by the tooling team.
tec-classify.how: Scanners read data in place, match it against patterns, dictionaries and machine-learning classifiers, and build an inventory of where each type of data sits and who can open it. Users and rules apply labels such as Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. DLP, DRM and access reviews use those labels.
pareto: A simple four-level label scheme that people understand
Scan the top file shares, Microsoft 365 or Google Drive, and the core customer databases first
Default labels on new documents, with user override and justification
Fix open access (everyone or anyone-with-link) on files that contain personal data
Feed labels to DLP and to the DPDP data inventory and retention schedule

tec-dam.summary: Database activity monitoring (DAM) records and alerts on who reads or changes sensitive data in databases; data masking replaces real values in test and development copies.
tec-dam.protects: Customer, account and card data in core databases; against privileged insider misuse, stolen DBA credentials, SQL injection and leaks from non-production copies.
tec-dam.placement: Agents on database servers, or network sensors on the database segment, reporting to a collector in the security zone; masking runs in the pipeline that refreshes test environments. Owned by the CISO with the database team.
tec-dam.how: Agents or sensors capture every SQL statement against monitored databases, including those of DBAs, independent of the database's own logs. Policies flag mass reads, off-hours access and access to sensitive columns, and can block in some modes. Masking tools find sensitive columns and replace values consistently so test data stays usable but is not real.
pareto: Monitor privileged and DBA access on the five to ten databases holding customer and payment data
Alert on bulk extraction and access from unusual accounts or hosts
Separate DAM administration from DBAs (segregation of duties)
Mask every non-production copy of production data before it leaves production
Send DAM alerts to the SIEM and review privileged activity monthly

tec-drm.summary: Digital rights management (DRM) wraps a document in encryption and rules, so only named people can open, edit, print or forward it, even after it leaves the organisation.
tec-drm.protects: Board papers, legal, strategy, M&A and regulator correspondence, customer files shared with partners; against forwarding, leaks by recipients and loss after sharing.
tec-drm.placement: A policy server (cloud or on premises) plus an add-in or viewer on user devices; integrations with email, document management and file sharing. Owned by the CISO with the Company Secretary and Legal for the first use cases.
tec-drm.how: When a document is protected, it is encrypted and tagged with a policy naming who may do what, and for how long. Opening it checks with the policy server, which can revoke access later. Every open is logged.
pareto: Start with Board, legal and strategy documents and a small user group
Automatic protection for documents leaving through email or the document management system
Browser-based viewing for external recipients so they need no install
Revoke access when a deal ends or a person leaves
Usage logs reviewed for the most sensitive documents

tec-forensics.summary: Digital forensics is the ability to collect, preserve and analyse evidence from devices, logs and cloud accounts, so the real cause of an incident is known and the evidence holds up.
tec-forensics.protects: The organisation's ability to prove what happened, to regulators, insurers, courts and the Board; supports recovery, disciplinary action and claims.
tec-forensics.placement: A process owned by the incident response lead; a forensic triage tool deployable to endpoints; a small evidence lab (write blockers, storage, chain-of-custody forms); and a retainer with an external forensics firm for major incidents.
tec-forensics.how: On an incident, responders collect volatile data and triage artefacts from affected hosts, image disks or cloud accounts where needed, and record chain of custody. Analysts build a timeline from endpoint, log and network evidence. Large or legal cases go to the retained firm, which reports findings that can support a legal case.
pareto: A signed retainer with a forensics firm with agreed response times, before you need it

Logs kept 180 days and protected from tampering (CERT-In direction), so there is evidence to analyse
A chain-of-custody procedure and an evidence store with hashing
An annual drill that runs a scenario end to end, including CERT-In 6-hour reporting

tec-pqc.summary: Quantum-safe readiness means knowing where the organisation uses cryptography and moving it, step by step, to the new post-quantum algorithms before quantum computers can break today's ones.
tec-pqc.protects: Long-lived confidential data (customer records, loan and KYC files, strategy) against 'harvest now, decrypt later' capture; digital signatures and PKI trust against future forgery.
tec-pqc.placement: A programme owned by the security architect, run across PKI, network (TLS, VPN), HSMs, applications and vendors; discovery tools scan code, hosts and network traffic.
tec-pqc.how: First build a cryptographic inventory (a cryptographic bill of materials, CBOM): which algorithms, keys, certificates and libraries are used where. Rank systems by how long their data must stay secret and how hard they are to change. Then adopt hybrid key exchange (classical plus ML-KEM) where products support it, require PQC roadmaps from vendors, and make systems crypto-agile so algorithms can be swapped.
pareto: A cryptographic inventory (CBOM) of external TLS, VPN, PKI, HSMs and core applications
Turn on hybrid TLS key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) where browsers, CDNs and OpenSSL 3.5+ already support it
PQC readiness and CBOM clauses in every new purchase and renewal
HSM and PKI roadmap for ML-KEM and ML-DSA (FIPS 203 and 204)
A migration plan that meets India's DST task force milestones for enterprises (foundations by 2028, high-priority systems by 2030, full adoption by 2033)
